title: Aurum Alpha browser error report
description: What a browser client sends when something fails in the page. Governed by standards/web-client.md WC5. An error reporter is a pipe to a third party and a report is written from the one context that holds everything the user typed, so what this shape EXCLUDES is as load-bearing as what it requires: no session cookie, no token, no personal data. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

ts.description: When the failure happened, in the fleet's canonical instant form (IP4) — not a locale-formatted string, per WC4.

kind.description: The class of failure. Per SC2's reason-giving rule this names the class and is never the whole report: 'message' carries this occurrence's specific reason.

message.description: THIS occurrence's specific reason — which operation, against which endpoint, with which value. A class of problem with no occurrence in it is the SC2 failure on a new surface, so a bare 'error occurred' fails review even though it validates here.

request_id.description: The id the server returned, from the problem+json envelope (http.md HA3). REQUIRED when kind is api_error — it is the whole correlation mechanism, and a report of a failed API call without it is a dead end. The browser does not originate the server's trace (WC5), so this, not a traceparent, is the handle.

build.description: Which bundle produced this. Required because browsers hold stale bundles far longer than servers hold stale builds, and a stack trace against unknown source is unreadable.

context.description: Non-identifying circumstances of the failure. Deliberately narrow: a route PATTERN rather than a resolved URL, because a resolved URL carries ids and often search terms.

route.description: The matched route pattern, e.g. '/invoices/:id' — never the resolved path.

problem_type.description: The problem+json 'type' URI, which is the stable class a client branches on (HA3).

stack.description: The stack trace, where one exists. Never present for kind 'api_error', where the failure is the server's and the stack would only show the fetch wrapper.

then.description: An api_error without the server's request id cannot be joined to anything (WC5).
